note: First 2 layers: plain windowed attention, no compression.
Eqs 9-10: per-raw-token KV/weight projections feeding the m=4-to-1 compression (SIMPLIFIED: linear cost, softmax-combine coefficient not modeled).
Eqs 13-14: low-rank down/up projection for indexer queries, FP4.
Eq 16: index score vs. every compressed block -- this is the term that scales with context length L, analogous to global attention's linear-in-L cost in the spec-decode workload.
Eq 17: top-512 selector over compressed indexer scores.
MQA over top-512 selected compressed entries + 128-token sliding window, shared K/V across all 64 query heads.
8 groups -> 1024-dim intermediate -> combine to d_model (SIMPLIFIED two-matmul stand-in for the per-group einsum).
No sparse selection -- dense MQA over ALL compressed entries (L/128) plus the 128-token sliding window.
Matches the paper's own stated per-expert cost exactly: 6*h*d FLOPs/token-expert-pair (Section 3.1) -- good cross-check on the general matmul-decomposition recipe.
THE real stochastic branch: affinity score per token over 256 routed experts, then top-6 selected. Needs a routing histogram from profiling to characterize which experts, not just how many.
Top-6 selection over the affinity scores.
6 of 256 experts fire per token, chosen by the router above. Weights are FP4 (post-training QAT, Section 5.2.1), dequantized to FP8 for the actual matmul -- modeled here at FP4 read bytes.

NOT stochastic: which experts a token hits is a deterministic hash of its token ID. Zero FLOPs, no profiling needed -- contrast directly with MOE.router_learned above, same layer TYPE, different (and non-probabilistic) selection mechanism.
Identical downstream compute to the learned-routing case.

NOT bandwidth- or compute-bound -- bound by 20 sequential dependent steps. See explanation.txt for why this needs a new resource axis (sequential depth x round-trip latency) instead of the compute/bandwidth roofline every other kernel here uses.

MTP depth=1: one extra lookahead-token prediction. This is what vLLM/SGLang attach speculative decoding to (branded 'DSpark' on the model card) -- reuse specdecode_kernels.py's B/C/D loop shape on TOP of this if modeling the full inference-serving DAG rather than just one forward pass.
